newsitem.title: SPAIN: French vote keeps Spain Ibex option vols sky high.
newsitem.headline: French vote keeps Spain Ibex option vols sky high.

text.p: The French vote for the left prompted a rebound in option volatility on the Spanish IBEX-35 share index to historic highs on Monday amid nervous trade.

Implied volatility, which rises as expectations of sharp moves grow, rebounded to 33 percent in "at the money" June maturities -- just slightly beneath last Thursday's record of 34 percent -- before retreating slightly again to 31 percent.
In the final vote Sunday, French Socialists won 240 seats but need 289 for an absolute majority, which has concerned markets worried about European progress toward a common currency.
Option dealers said trade was thin in the morning, making it difficult to measure the depth of the moves although they added the French election results generated nerves.
"This morning we saw a rebound in volatility from the French election, but now we have corrected by two points since the open," said the chief of derivatives at a French brokerage in Madrid.
"Personally I think that one cannot consider the short-term reaction to the French vote and we will have to wait to see (the future cabinet and its EMU stance) to judge the real effect."

Earlier in the day, Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister said the result of the French election had changed the EMU environment and signalled that the project could enter into "rougher waters" ahead.
The German discussion on a possible revaluation of Bundesbank gold reserves is also weighing on the market.
"People are pretty watchful of what is happening in German," the derivatives chief said.
In recent weeks, worries of sharp moves after a series of new highs in the IBEX prompted a substantial rise in options acitivity and prices.
Dealers said option prices were likely to remain high given the current climate.
"I don't think we can see a decline in volatility despite the sharp recent rise," a dealer said.
"There are many doubts in the air, and the people are carefully watching Germany, France and monetary union."
